memory_update.text: In this candidate chunk, AMAT, MRVL, COHR, LITE, ENTG, and LRCX are closer to Serenity-style physical supply-chain bottlenecks than MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, ORCL, and SNOW, which are mainly demand aggregators or monetization layers.

AMAT has the strongest explicit AI semicap evidence in this chunk because current 2026 materials tie leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM/HBM, and advanced packaging to AI performance-per-watt and WFE growth.

MRVL has strong direct mapping to AI optical interconnect and custom silicon through 1.6T optical DSPs, coherent DCI products, and AI data-center connectivity positioning; future work should separate optical DSP, custom XPU, Ethernet, and DCI revenue drivers.
COHR and LITE are optical-component candidates where bottleneck status depends on AI datacom mix, 800G/1.6T qualification, InP/laser capacity, yields, and hyperscaler/NVIDIA-linked customer evidence.

MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, and ORCL should be tracked as capex and cloud-demand validators; their relationship to the theme is strongest when capex commitments, capacity constraints, and AI workload monetization pull through demand to accelerators, HBM, optics, networking, power, and data-center construction.

SNOW belongs to the enterprise AI data layer, not the physical compute chokepoint layer; its research question is whether AI Data Cloud products create incremental consumption and retention rather than only thematic positioning.
Need primary-source validation for ENTG's AI-specific exposure: quantify revenue or management commentary tied to HBM, EUV, advanced nodes, advanced packaging, and contamination-control demand.
Need LRCX FY2026 earnings-call evidence distinguishing AI-related HBM/DRAM/foundry/advanced-packaging tool demand from broader wafer-fab equipment cyclicality and China/export-control exposure.

Need customer-level or segment-level evidence for COHR and LITE to test whether optics demand is capacity-constrained and margin-accretive, or vulnerable to hyperscaler inventory cycles and price pressure.
Need market-pricing check in a later layer: compare expected AI revenue/capex growth versus current valuation and consensus assumptions without producing buy/sell recommendations or price targets.

summary: This Layer 2B mapping links the candidate chunk to AI infrastructure demand and supply-chain nodes. The chunk separates into four relationship groups: upstream process/material chokepoints (ENTG, LRCX, AMAT), optical/custom-connectivity chokepoints (MRVL, COHR, LITE), hyperscale demand aggregators and custom-silicon buyers (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, ORCL), and enterprise AI data-layer monetization (SNOW). Highest Serenity relevance in this chunk comes from companies closest to hard-to-qualify physical supply-chain nodes: contamination control/materials, etch/deposition/process tools, advanced packaging/HBM enablement, optical DSPs, lasers, transceivers, and photonic components. Cloud/software tickers are important demand validators but generally weaker bottleneck owners unless evidence shows proprietary infrastructure, constrained capacity, or differentiated AI monetization.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check FY2025 10-K, latest 2026 quarterly earnings, segment disclosures for Advanced Purity Solutions and Materials Solutions, customer concentration, advanced-node/HBM commentary, capex plans, and whether management explicitly ties demand to AI logic, HBM, EUV, or advanced packaging.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Entegris maps to ultra-clean materials, filtration, purification, specialty materials, and wafer-handling inputs that support advanced-node logic, memory, EUV process steps, CMP, and advanced packaging yield. The relationship is bottleneck-relevant because contamination-control suppliers can face long customer qualification cycles and high switching costs, but AI-specific revenue mix and customer pull-through need validation.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate with FY2026 filings and earnings transcripts: WFE exposure by memory/foundry/logic, HBM-specific tool demand, advanced packaging revenue contribution, backlog, China/export-control sensitivity, and whether AI-driven DRAM/foundry spending is offset by non-AI wafer-fab cyclicality.
ticker_relationships.node: Semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment: etch, deposition, clean, and advanced packaging
ticker_relationships.relationship: Lam Research maps to wafer-fab equipment needed for advanced memory, logic, and packaging structures. It is a second-order AI infrastructure beneficiary because HBM, leading-edge logic, and advanced packaging require complex process steps where etch, deposition, strip, and clean tools can influence yield and capacity ramps.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track 2026 Semiconductor Systems growth, customer co-innovation with Micron and other memory/foundry customers, advanced packaging revenue, order momentum, export-control impact, and whether AI-driven WFE demand remains durable after current capacity additions.
ticker_relationships.node: Semiconductor equipment and materials engineering for leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, and advanced packaging
ticker_relationships.relationship: Applied Materials maps broadly to materials engineering, deposition, process control, metrology, and advanced packaging equipment. The relationship is stronger than a generic semicap read-through because Applied explicitly frames leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM/HBM, and advanced packaging as AI performance-per-watt enablers and 2026 WFE growth drivers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate AI revenue split across custom silicon, optical DSPs, switching, and electro-optics; identify customer concentration risk; confirm 1.6T sampling-to-volume timing; compare design-win durability against Broadcom and in-house hyperscaler silicon.
ticker_relationships.node: AI custom silicon, optical DSPs, SerDes, Ethernet/data-center interconnect
ticker_relationships.relationship: Marvell maps to AI connectivity and custom silicon: optical DSPs for 800G/1.6T transitions, coherent DCI products, custom XPU programs, and high-speed data infrastructure silicon. Its relationship is bottleneck-plausible where AI clusters need faster optical links and hyperscalers diversify compute architecture beyond merchant GPUs.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest FY2026 financial release and investor presentations for AI datacom revenue, 800G and 1.6T mix, customer concentration, InP capacity ramp status, pricing, yields, and whether orders are binding or inventory-driven.
ticker_relationships.node: Optical communications components, transceivers, lasers, InP/photonics capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: Coherent maps to AI data-center optics through transceivers, optical components, photonics materials, lasers, and related capacity. Its relationship is bottleneck-plausible because AI cluster scale increases demand for 800G/1.6T optical links and may pressure InP, laser, and high-speed transceiver manufacturing capacity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate cloud/data-center revenue mix, AI optics backlog, 800G/1.6T product qualification, customer concentration, gross margin impact from mix shift, and capacity expansion plans.
ticker_relationships.node: Photonic components, lasers, optical switching, and data-center optical supply chain
ticker_relationships.relationship: Lumentum maps to AI data-center optical demand through components such as EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, 800G modules, and optical switching. The relationship is relevant but needs validation because the company also has non-AI telecom/industrial/consumer exposure and may be more component-level than full-system bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track quarterly capex including finance leases, Azure AI capacity constraints, AI revenue or workload disclosures, gross margin pressure from depreciation and memory prices, and whether spend is converting into durable cloud revenue.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale AI demand aggregation: Azure, cloud infrastructure capex, enterprise copilots
ticker_relationships.relationship: Microsoft is a primary demand validator for AI infrastructure through Azure, enterprise AI software, and large cloud capex. It does not usually own the narrow physical bottleneck, but its capex, capacity-constraint commentary, and finance-lease commitments can pull through demand for accelerators, HBM, optics, networking, power equipment, and data centers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate Q1/Q2 2026 capex and technical infrastructure disclosures, TPU roadmap and external availability, Google Cloud AI revenue contribution, capacity constraints, and financing plans for AI infrastructure.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale AI demand aggregation and custom accelerator ecosystem: Google Cloud, TPU, Search/AI infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Alphabet maps to AI infrastructure demand through Google Cloud, Search AI, Gemini/DeepMind workloads, TPU deployment, and technical infrastructure capex. It is a demand-side validator and custom-silicon buyer, with potential read-through to HBM, foundry, packaging, networking, power, and data-center construction.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track AWS AI revenue run-rate disclosures if repeated, Trainium/Inferentia adoption, capex and finance-lease commitments, AWS operating margin, data-center capacity constraints, and supplier relationships for networking, optics, HBM, and foundry.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale AI demand aggregation and custom accelerator ecosystem: AWS, Trainium, Inferentia, cloud infrastructure

ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale AI demand aggregation: AI training/inference, recommendation systems, GenAI, ad tools, data centers
ticker_relationships.relationship: Meta maps to AI infrastructure demand through large-scale training, inference, AI-powered ad systems, recommender systems, Meta AI, and data-center/server/network capex. It is a major demand-side read-through for accelerators, HBM, networking, optics, power, and data-center capacity rather than a direct physical bottleneck supplier.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate remaining performance obligations, OCI revenue growth, AI contract backlog quality, capex funding needs, utilization, gross margin trajectory, and dependence on a small number of AI customers or GPU suppliers.
ticker_relationships.node: AI cloud infrastructure and enterprise cloud capacity: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Oracle maps to AI infrastructure demand through OCI growth, GPU cluster/cloud capacity, enterprise workloads, and large AI cloud contracts. It is a useful non-mega-hyperscaler demand validator and may indicate how AI compute demand extends beyond Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check FY2026 product revenue growth, net revenue retention, AI Data Cloud usage metrics, Cortex/agentic AI adoption, customer-count expansion, consumption trends, and whether AI products drive new workloads or cannibalize existing warehouse spend.
ticker_relationships.node: Enterprise AI data layer: cloud data platform, analytics, governance, application development
ticker_relationships.relationship: Snowflake maps to enterprise AI software demand rather than physical AI infrastructure bottlenecks. Its relationship is that AI adoption requires governed enterprise data, analytics, and application infrastructure; the key question is whether Snowflake captures incremental AI workloads and platform spend instead of merely rebranding existing data-cloud demand.
